principles.statement: Write the failing test that describes the missing behavior before writing the behavior.
principles.rationale: A test written after the code tests what the code does; a test written before tests what the code SHOULD do — and survives as the spec.

principles.statement: Red, green, refactor: fail first for the right reason, pass minimally, then clean up with the test as the safety net.
principles.rationale: Skipping the red step leaves you unable to distinguish a passing test from a broken one.

principles.statement: One behavioral change per test — a test asserting three things fails ambiguously.
principles.rationale: A failing multi-assert test doesn't tell you which behavior broke.

heuristics.name: Test the contract, not the implementation
heuristics.description: Assert observable outputs and state changes, never internal call sequences.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Writing any test against a function or service.

heuristics.name: Name tests as behavior sentences
heuristics.description: 'refresh_marks_stale_file_refs' says what it verifies; 'test_refresh_2' says nothing.
examples: When the test name completes the sentence 'this test verifies that…', the name is right.

decision_rules.condition: A bug report arrives with a reproducible defect.
decision_rules.action: Write the failing test that reproduces it FIRST — it becomes the regression guard for the fix.

decision_rules.condition: A test cannot be written because the design makes the behavior untestable.
decision_rules.action: That is a design defect — refactor for testability before implementing, not a reason to skip the test.
